request.text: Please rewrite this so it sounds neighborly rather than accusing, keep it to two sentences, and don't call the dog aggressive: Your dog keeps squeezing through the hedge and trampling my seedlings. Fix your fence.

responsibilities.outcome: Produce a courteous reformulation of no more than two sentences that preserves the report of the neighbor's dog entering through the hedge, the damage to seedlings, and a request to secure the boundary without labeling the dog aggressive.

semantic_facts: The response should consist only of a neighborly reformulation in no more than two sentences.
It should retain the material problem—dog entry through the hedge and trampled seedlings—and politely ask the neighbor to secure the fence or hedge boundary.
forbidden_claims: The reformulation calls the dog aggressive, malicious, or dangerous without evidence.
The assistant claims the message was sent or invents prior complaints, motives, injuries, or agreements.

target.claim_boundary: assistant-authored candidate oracle; not independently reviewed

negative_hypotheses: Politeness optimization erases the concrete damage or the request that the boundary be secured.
The planner mistakes text reformulation for authorization to contact the neighbor or perform a physical intervention.
